limitations: No discovered theorem or RL training
proposed_simulation_invariant: Atoms0..256 map identically. Seed nodes are loaded first, exactly and without duplicates.

Physical HEAP additionally stores immutable program metadata and captured argument lists. The proposed injection maps each original value to its canonical structural representative, preserving pair constructors and both children.
Each instruction sees corresponding semantic register values, program instruction, next PC and full call frames. No opcode observes numeric pair IDs as integers.
Canonical cons may reuse a node created for metadata or argument storage without changing its mathematical value.
A finite accepting trace would require root return exactly atom1, not merely a halted helper or empty caller stack.

Actual unknown-certificate search, learned certified markings, inventory/receptor family learning, and matched conventional/GCTS/RL comparisons remain open.

opcodes.manual_argument: Capture destination and constant index, select complete immutable constants list by physical index; write actual constant reference after all operands are captured.
opcodes.name: const

opcodes.manual_argument: Read source register before destructive register write; source and destination may coincide.
opcodes.name: move

opcodes.manual_argument: Read both source references before any write; canonical_cons preserves both and returns canonical node reference.
opcodes.name: cons

opcodes.manual_argument: Read source; heap lookup rejects atom/nil and returns the actual left child; destination may alias source.
opcodes.name: head

opcodes.manual_argument: Read source; heap lookup rejects atom/nil and returns the actual right child.
opcodes.name: tail

opcodes.manual_argument: Canonical references at most \(256\) are atoms, including nil. Greater references are nodes under the complete register and heap invariant.
opcodes.name: pair

opcodes.manual_argument: Both references must be atoms including nil, then exact equality; equal node references return false.
opcodes.name: atom

opcodes.manual_argument: Require a byte atom in \(\{0,\ldots,254\}\), then add \(1\). Byte \(255\), nil \(256\) and pairs are refused.
opcodes.name: succ

opcodes.manual_argument: Require exactly Boolean atom \(0\) or \(1\), then invert it. Every other value is refused.
opcodes.name: not

opcodes.manual_argument: Capture both target instructions before reading the condition register. Exactly \(0\) selects the first target and exactly \(1\) selects the second.
opcodes.name: branch

opcodes.manual_argument: Set PC to captured validated instruction index; fetch handles subsequent instruction.
opcodes.name: jump

opcodes.manual_argument: Capture destination/target and every caller argument value first, including duplicate indices. Turn the captured values into a canonical immutable list, pop FnMeta and destination, push full caller frame with already incremented PC, then build complete callee vector with nil padding and commit once.
opcodes.name: call

opcodes.manual_argument: Read the result before restoring a frame. A nonempty frame restores the complete caller and writes its saved destination once. With no caller, accept exactly atom \(1\).
opcodes.name: return
